classification.difficultyReason: In the hardest parts, identify the lateral-edge right triangle, use Pythagoras to recover height or half-diagonal, and calculate square-base area before pyramid volume.

content.prompt: Find the volume of each of these pyramids:

spec.description: Unshaded square-based pyramid with perpendicular height and front base side labelled.
spec.mathematics: Square base side 3 m; perpendicular height 3 m.

spec.description: Unshaded square-based pyramid with perpendicular height and front base side labelled.
spec.mathematics: Square base side 5 cm; perpendicular height 6 cm.

spec.description: Unshaded square-based pyramid; both measurements retain stacked fractions.
spec.mathematics: Square base side 3/2 m; perpendicular height 3/2 m.

spec.description: The 5 cm label belongs to the apex-to-base-vertex lateral edge, not a face altitude.
spec.mathematics: Perpendicular height 4 cm; lateral edge 5 cm; square base.

answer.short:
$24\,\mathrm{cm}^3$

Use Pythagoras to find half the base diagonal, then use $A=\frac12d^2$.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ be half the base diagonal.
$$\begin{align*}x&=\sqrt{5^2-4^2}\\x&=3\,\mathrm{cm}\\A&=\frac{(2x)^2}{2}\\A&=\frac{6^2}{2}=18\,\mathrm{cm}^2\\V&=\frac13(18)(4)\\V&=24\,\mathrm{cm}^3\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Full base diagonal connects opposite base vertices; height ends at its midpoint.
spec.mathematics: Full square-base diagonal 12 m; perpendicular height 10 m.

spec.description: The 4 cm segment runs from the base centre to a vertex and represents half the diagonal.
spec.mathematics: Lateral edge 6 cm; half base diagonal 4 cm; square base.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; perpendicular height remains unlabelled.

answer.short:
$\frac{64\sqrt5}{3}\,\mathrm{cm}^3$

Use Pythagoras for the height and double 4 cm to obtain the base diagonal.
